chapter: Return to New York, addiction, health and the NBC job
title: Back to New York in 1956 and the night Teddy Reig snored on the phone
summary: He left Los Angeles early; Reig left him stranded and snored through his call.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I said, 'I remember you. I played with you.' She said she was a drummer. I said, 'Did you ever play Jazz City?' She said, 'Yes.' I said, well I played my last job there in late '55, going into '56. I left town about a month early, before my probation was up. My probation officer told me that I didn't have to report back anymore, so I headed on back east, and then someone else told me that they had lifted this cabaret card thing, and I went back all happy, and

I called -- from the airport I called Teddy Rerg and told him that I was at La Guardia Airport and on my way to Philadelphia until my probation was up and then I'd be on into New York. He said, "Man, don't go to Philadelphia." He said, "They'll arrest you if you spit on the ground, and they have the blue law there, too, that you can't work on Sundays." He said, "You better come on into town. I'll send Ned out there." Well, Ned was Erroll Garner's valet, but he was working for Teddy now, at this time. So Ned shows up, I meet him at the Braddock. He was driving Teddy's car, but Teddy never showed up. I got a $14.00 rebate off of my ticket, as I didn't go to Philadelphia. But Teddy was supposed to come down and pick me up and give me some money to get me an apartment. He was going to loan me the money, you know. I waited and I waited, and Ned waited too. He said, "Well, man, I've got to go." He said, "You just get on the phone and continue calling him till you catch him at home." When I caught him at home, he was in bed asleep, and he answered the phone and started snoring in my ear, and I'm whistling and hollering and screaming and everything else, trying to wake him up. And he's snoring. I said, "Oh, this is really something." So I had to sit up in the Braddock Hotel lobby all night long. The next day I said, "Man, why would you do that to me." I said, "You didn't show up when you said you was going to show up, and then I get you on the phone, and you answer the phone and snore in my ear." He said, "Is that what happened?"

He said, "I noticed when I got up the phone was off the hook." He didn't remember even talking to me, even answering the phone. So I got together with him. He got me a few record dates on his label, Roost label. And he was recording -- like we were the house musicians. Cozy Cole and Sanford Gold Goal, a piano player. And --
